attributes.body:
In N5, we learned about the use of より that is seen when making comparisons in より～のほうが. However, in this lesson, we will take a look at how this case marking particle can be used by itself. When used alone, this particle expresses that (A) (a noun or verb) is being compared to (B) (a noun or verb that is regularly paired with an adjective). The word that より is directly attached to will always be 'less than' the comparison being made. However, the overall expression is used to describe that (B) is 'more' (something) than (A).

Caution

In many textbooks, より is taught as meaning 'more', but the word that より is attached to will actually be the thing that is 'less' (something). The word/quote that has が attached to it will be the thing that is 'more' (adjective). This is particularly confusing when より is not directly attached to a word, something which is common in casual spoken language.

In this sentence, because the が is attached to これ, これ is the thing that is 'more expensive'. As より is not actually directly connected to any other word, it therefore means that これ is expensive, compared to 'other things'. When you see より like this, just pretend that it says 'other things' before it.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: A is MORE / BETTER than B (comparison)

attributes.body: Both より and 以上に are used for comparisons. In some cases, their meaning and usage can overlap, e.g. 思っていたより and 思っていた以上に both mean 'more than I thought'. In other cases, they can differ in that 以上に suggests a shared quality between the two things being compared. For example, AはBより強い simply states that A is stronger than B, while AはB以上に強い suggests that A is even stronger than B (who is also strong).

second_relatable.title: 以上に
second_relatable.meaning: More than, No less than, Even more

attributes.body: より expresses a general comparison, like 'more than (A)' or '~er,' e.g. 月曜日より水曜日がいい ('Wednesday is better than Monday.') or 走るより野球をするのが好き ('I prefer playing baseball to running.'). In contrast, というより specifically means 'more/rather than saying (A)' and is used primarily when rephrasing or clarifying something.

second_relatable.title: というより
second_relatable.meaning: ...is more of a... than a..., Rather than saying that...

attributes.body: Both express comparison meaning ‘more than,’ and they can overlap in meaning, but the tone differs. にもまして is a more formal, literary variant often used in writing or speeches to emphasize that something exceeds another in degree, as in 昨年にもまして今年は暑い ('This year is even hotter than last year.'). より is the neutral, everyday comparative used broadly in speech and writing without added emphasis, as in 去年より今年の方が暑い ('This year is hotter than last year.').

first_relatable.title: にもまして
first_relatable.meaning: Even -er than, Even more than, More than anything, More than anybody, More than ever

attributes.body: より is used to make comparisons, with Xより meaning 'more than X.' It often appears in the pattern より～のほうが, as in 'More than X, Y is...' but can also be used without のほうが. In any case, より always follows the thing being compared as 'less.' It can also directly precede adjectives—for example, より高い ('more expensive [than something]'), even if the item being compared isn't stated.

より expresses a general comparison, like 'more than (A)' or '~er,' e.g. 月曜日より水曜日がいい ('Wednesday is better than Monday.') or 走るより野球をするのが好き ('I prefer playing baseball to running.'). In contrast, こそ adds emphasis, highlighting something as especially important, e.g. 月曜日こそ図書館に行きたい ('Monday is precisely when I want to go to the library.').

second_relatable.title: こそ
second_relatable.meaning: For sure, For certain, Even more so, Underlined or bolded text

attributes.body: Both 以上① and より express comparisons like 'more than (A)', but with different nuances. 以上 follows numbers or nouns like これ, and means '(A) or more,' e.g. ２時間以上かかる ('It will take two or more hours.'). より makes general comparisons and does not necessarily have a nuance of measuring some quantity.

first_relatable.title: 以上 ①
first_relatable.meaning: More than (or equal to), Over・(and) above, Any more・Greater, Exceeding

attributes.body: Both expressions are used for comparisons. ほど～ない makes negative comparisons, e.g. ジョンはトムほど強くない ('John isn't as strong as Tom.'). より is used for positive comparisons, e.g. トムはジョンより強い ('Tom is stronger than John.'). Note that ほど follows the greater of the two options, while より follows the lesser.
